An automated Python pipeline driven by Claude and TTS now compiles offline-ready HTML materials with embedded screenshots, synchronized voiceovers and bilingual support in under 30 minutes. Challenge High manual overhead: structuring text, translating multi-step guides, logging video timestamps and aligning voiceovers took hours per lecture. d: Welcome to the Pumpkin-Heads family.
x: art portfolio Welcome Pumpkin-Heads family On the edge of a misty forest, where summer meets eternal twilight, lives the Pumpkinhead family. They weren’t born; they grew from seeds of ancient magic and a sincere love for Halloween. The elders make sure the candles inside never go out, for that inner glow is their very soul. They are the guardians of coziness during the coldest season. When November comes, they don’t vanish but simply fall asleep beneath the leaves, dreaming of ripe berries and autumn rains, waiting for their time to grace your postcards once again.

d: How pigeonpolly.com handles your data.
x: privacy Privacy Short and honest: what this site keeps about you, why, and how to get it deleted. Last updated: 17 October 2026. Who is responsible Alina Otkinska (Pigeon Polly Art Lab), Riga, Latvia. You can reach me through the Write to me form. Just visiting The site is hosted by Cloudflare . Visits are counted by the site itself, with no cookies and no personal profiles: page address, the site you came from, device type, browser, country (from Cloudflare) and a code that changes every day so that one person is counted once per day. The same way (no names, no cookies) the site counts steps like “opened the sign-in window” and “signed in”. Your IP address is not stored. The data is kept for about 13 months. Cloudflare may keep short technical logs (like IP addresses) for security. On the Daily Challenge page, the photo you add for a share card stays in your browser and is never uploaded. Your settings (level, black & white mode) are saved only in your browser. Forms When you use Write to me , your message and e-mail are delivered to my inbox through FormSubmit . I use them only to reply, and delete them on request. Your account (sign-in on any page) You sign in with Google or with an e-mail and password . From Google I receive your Google account ID and e-mail address. I store: your Google account ID and/or e-mail, only to sign you in (never shown to anyone); if you use a password: only a scrambled, salted code of it (PBKDF2 hash), never the password itself, and the date you agreed to these rules; your nickname (required: you choose it right after your first sign-in), the sketches you upload, their dates and themes; the time of your last visit (rounded to about 10 minutes), to show recent visitors in the flock on the home page; the language of the site pages you open and whether you want Wobbleland holiday emails : on each Wobbleland holiday your bird gets a gift, and if you signed in with an e-mail, a short greeting is sent to it (through the Resend mail service). You can turn them off in your profile or with the link in any such email; your consent to show sketches publicly; one sign-in cookie ( pp_s ) that keeps you logged in for up to 180 days. Public, visible to everyone on the site: your nickname and your profile with sketches, streak, level and badges; your pixel bird (or cat, or crow) with your nickname in the flock on the home page; your nickname next to your blog comments. Private: your e-mail and the time of your last visit. By signing in you agree that your nickname is public, so please don’t use your real full name if you don’t want to. What other birds see: your nickname, your bird and your room (what stands in it); your sketches (except hidden ones); feathers: other birds see how many feathers your room has, and you, as the owner, see who visited your room and who left a feather (nicknames). Flock news (/flock/news/ and the home page) shows short lines with your nickname and a link to your profile: you joined the flock, drew the sketch of the day, got 3 or more new things in your room, a badge, a collectible card, a legendary item, solved every 10th Titos case, your sketch became “Polly’s choice”, your room got 10 feathers. News is kept for 30 days. Blocked birds and hidden sketches are never shown. You can hide yourself from the news in your profile (“Don’t show me in the flock news”). Why I may do this: to provide the service you asked for, including the public nickname and the flock (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)) and, for showing your sketches publicly, your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)). You can withdraw it at any time by deleting a sketch or your whole account. How long: your sketches stay while you are active. If you neither upload anything nor visit the site for more than 3 months, your sketches may be deleted automatically, but only when the storage is almost full (oldest inactivity first); your nickname, best streak and badges stay so you can come back. Your account stays until you delete it. Deleting the account remov

d: Wobbleland: an island of eleven towns drawn in pixels. Explore the interactive map and meet every town with Polly as your guide.
x: an illustrated island Welcome to Wobbleland! Greetings, dear reader. My name is Polly, and I am a pigeon. Though, to be entirely precise, I am not quite an ordinary representative of my species. I suppose in our world, no one is surprised by a bird capable of holding a conversation over a cup of strong morning coffee or critically reviewing the latest literary releases with a look on her face, if, of course, a pigeon can be said to have a face. My life, much like the life of Wobbleland itself, is a sequence of small oddities that have become second nature. But if you do not mind the company of a feathered guide with a sharp beak and an even sharper eye for things, I shall be your guide. After all, who else is going to tell you about our island the way a bird would, one who is accustomed to seeing everything from the height of a ledge and knows a little more about city secrets than any self-respecting townsperson ought to? — Polly, your feathered guide 🗺 Explore the map 📖 Recipe book 📅 Holiday calendar Polly’s Recipe Book Ripple Tickle Sea Eleven towns, one wobble Tap a crest on the map, or a town below, to open its page.
